title: Invaract Data Contract
description: Structural shape of a contract document Invaract's `contract` module (com.invaract.contract.ContractParser/ContractValidator) accepts, modeled after the Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS) - see docs/CONTRACT_MODEL.md. This schema is deliberately permissive at every level (`additionalProperties: true`) to match the parser's own design: an unrecognized key is preserved verbatim rather than rejected, so a contract authored for other ODCS-based tooling stays valid input here too. It also intentionally sits between two layers of the real Scala implementation: some constraints here (id, version, dataset name/location/schema, field name/type) mirror ContractParser's hard parse failures; others (outputs being present and non-empty, a schema's fields being non-empty) mirror ContractValidator's Error-level checks rather than the parser alone, because a document that merely parses but fails validation isn't a useful contract either. Two things this schema does NOT and cannot enforce, both still Scala-side responsibilities: duplicate-name detection (dataset names, field names) and cross-field business rules (e.g. ContractValidator's required-and-nullable warning) - see docs/CONTRACT_MODEL.md's "JSON Schema" section for the full list of what's schema-level versus what stays engine-only.

id.description: Contract identity. Must be non-empty (ContractParser hard failure otherwise). ContractValidator additionally warns (not an error) if it doesn't start with a letter and contain only alphanumerics, '.', '_', '-' - not enforced here since the parser still accepts other values.

version.description: MAJOR.MINOR[.PATCH], e.g. "1.0.0" or "1.0" (PATCH defaults to 0). Any other shape is a ContractParser hard failure (ContractVersion.parse).

status.description: Free-form; Invaract does not constrain or interpret this value. Defaults to "active" if the key is omitted.

inputs.description: Datasets this transformation reads from. Optional - omitted or empty means no declared inputs.

outputs.description: Datasets this transformation writes to. Required and non-empty: a contract with no outputs parses but fails ContractValidator with an Error ("Contract must declare at least one output dataset"), so this schema requires it up front rather than accepting a document ContractValidator would immediately reject.

rules.description: Declarative rules attached to the contract. Most rule types (e.g. compatibility mode) are recorded but not yet verified against a transformation - see ROADMAP.md. Three types ARE interpreted and enforced during verification (com.invaract.contract.RuleType/ContractRule.interpret, checked by spark-adapter's RuleVerifier against a real Spark row-level DML operation): 'merge_condition' (columns: a MERGE's ON clause must reference these), 'forbid_unconditional_delete' (no properties: a DELETE may never omit a filtering predicate), and 'allowed_update_columns' (columns: an UPDATE may only assign these). A known rule type with malformed properties for its shape is a ContractValidator Error, not silently ignored.

extensions.description: Explicit bucket for metadata Invaract doesn't interpret (owners, SLAs, quality rules, ...). Any top-level key not listed in this schema's `properties` is preserved here too by ContractParser, whether or not it's nested under this explicit `extensions` map.

name.description: Logical name used to look up this dataset (Contract.input/output). Must be unique within inputs and within outputs - not enforced by this schema, only by ContractValidator.

location.description: Physical location: table name, file path, topic, etc.

format.description: Optional storage/serialization format, e.g. "table", "parquet", "delta". Not a closed set - any value is accepted.

saveMode.description: Optional expected write behavior for an output dataset, e.g. "append", "overwrite", "ignore", "error". Meaningless for an input dataset; only checked by StructuralVerifier against a plan's Write node. Not a closed set.

fields.description: The 'fields' key itself is a ContractParser hard requirement; a dataset schema with zero fields parses but fails ContractValidator with an Error ("Schema must declare at least one field"), so this schema requires at least one up front.

name.description: Field name. Must be unique among sibling fields (within the same schema, or the same struct's properties) - not enforced by this schema, only by ContractValidator.

type.description: Field type. Recognized values (ContractValidator.KnownTypes): string, integer, long, short, byte, double, float, decimal, boolean, date, timestamp, binary, struct, array, map. An unrecognized value is only a ContractValidator Warning, not a parse or validation Error, so it is not enforced here as an enum - a contract using a type this version of Invaract doesn't yet know about still parses and still matches this schema. A field with a non-empty `properties` array is treated as a struct regardless of this value.

required.description: Whether the field must be present. Defaults to false if omitted.

nullable.description: Whether the field's value may be null when present. Defaults to the opposite of `required` if omitted (i.e. a required field defaults to non-nullable). ContractValidator warns, but does not error, if both `required` and `nullable` are explicitly true together.

properties.description: Nested fields, for a struct/record type. A field with a non-empty `properties` list is treated as a struct regardless of its declared `type`.

sensitivityTags.description: Open-vocabulary governance labels for this field (e.g. "pii", "financial", "restricted") - Invaract does not define or restrict which tags exist. spark-adapter's SensitivityLineage propagates whichever tags an input field carries to every output column that transitively derives from it, for audit/governance visibility - this is reporting, not enforcement, so a tagged field does not by itself cause verification to fail. A non-list value for this key is a ContractParser hard failure, not silently ignored.

type.description: Rule kind, e.g. "compatibility", "merge_condition", "forbid_unconditional_delete", "allowed_update_columns". Every other key on a rule object is rule-specific and captured verbatim (ContractRule.properties). Only the latter three are interpreted and enforced today (see RuleType/ContractRule.interpret) - every other rule type is recorded but not yet verified (see ROADMAP.md).
